title: Policy checkpoint catalog — multi-region routing & authz heuristics (draft)
content:
Purpose:
This is a working catalog of candidate enforcement checkpoints for routing and control plane authz in multi-region Redwood deployments. Goal is to surface tradeoffs for placement (edge vs control-plane vs serving), preferred policy model (ABAC vs RBAC for each checkpoint), expected latency impact, and test/observability requirements. Not a final design — a pragmatic catalogue to inform implementation choices and an experiment matrix for canary rollouts.

Background/context:
- We run a region-aware routing fabric with global control plane decisioning for policy and a set of region-local routers and serving pools.
- Customers can use hosted, dedicated, or private deployments; enforcement surfaces differ per mode.
- We need predictable SLOs for latency while meeting enterprise compliance (auditable denies, attribute-based segmentation).

High-level principles that guided this catalog:
1) Fail-safe semantics must be explicit: for each checkpoint, decide fail-open vs fail-closed.
2) Put low-latency, high-frequency checks near the data path (edge or router) and heavyweight attribute resolution in the control plane or sidecars with caching.
3) Prefer deterministic, easy-to-audit decisions for compliance-critical flows (RBAC templates with ABAC overrides where necessary).
4) Observability and test harness must attach to each checkpoint so policy regressions are detectable and reversible.

Checkpoint catalog (candidate enforcement points):
- Ingress edge gateway (region-local):
  - Responsibility: quick allow/deny for basic tenancy, API key validity, coarse RBAC role checks (e.g., org-level admin vs non-admin).
  - Model: RBAC primary (fast lookup), with ABAC tags allowed when pre-cached.
  - Latency impact: sub-ms to low ms; should not call external PDP on hot path.
  - Fail semantics: fail-open for public non-critical read endpoints, fail-closed for admin/management APIs.
  - Observability: request-scoped decision-id header, sample request/decision pairs to policy-log stream.

- Regional routing plane (route selection / capacity-aware fallback):
  - Responsibility: region affinity, tenant isolation enforcement at routing layer (prevent cross-tenant traffic when isolation required), route-level quotas and burst enforcement.
  - Model: mixed — static RBAC for route-level schema + ABAC for dynamic quota attributes (e.g., tokens_consumed_today).
  - Latency: moderate; can tolerate an extra 1–3ms if cached attributes used.
  - Fail semantics: fail-open for routing fallback pathways (route to lower-tier model) but emit alert and increment policy-regression metric.

- Control plane PDP (centralized policy decision point):
  - Responsibility: canonical policy evaluation (full ABAC expressions, delegations, custom claim resolution), policy authoring and rollouts, policy delta propagation.
  - Model: ABAC-first (supports expressive rules against attributes from identity provider, entitlements, resource metadata).
  - Latency: not on hot path for user requests; used to seed caches and to evaluate uncommon / complex decisions.
  - Fail semantics: read-only for policy store during outage; local caches decide according to last-known-good with TTL and tombstone semantics.
  - Observability: complete decision logs retained for audit (request-id, input attributes, policy-version, decision).

- Serving node (per-model process / worker):
  - Responsibility: final runtime guard for model invocation; enforce tenant quota at token-level, enforce content-level flags (e.g., PII redaction required), and last-mile authz checks for data egress.
  - Model: Lightweight RBAC/allowlist checks + inline attribute checks from local cache (e.g., tenant policy flags).
  - Latency: must be micro-optimized; use in-process caches and precompiled policy lambdas.
  - Fail semantics: fail-closed for data exfiltration checks; fail-open for non-security throttles with alerting.

- Admin/control APIs (control plane endpoints):
  - Responsibility: role management, rollout triggers, key rotation.
  - Model: strict RBAC with 2FA/SCW governance checks; ABAC used only to compute delegation scopes.
  - Latency: administrative, not latency-sensitive.
  - Fail semantics: always fail-closed on ambiguous authz inputs.

Policy model recommendations per checkpoint:
- Edge/Ingress: use coarse RBAC roles precomputed in the identity token (minimizes attribute lookups). Represent critical flags as short-lived claims injected by upstream authn.
- Router/Region: support dynamic attributes with local attribute caches (KV backed by regional store). Maintain a policy version header so routers can detect stale policies.
- Control plane PDP: express full ABAC, support policy authoring DSL, provide pre-compiled decision graphs to downstreams.
- Serving nodes: compile safe subset of ABAC into tiny decision DAGs suitable for execution in-process. Avoid invoking remote PDP on hot path.

Attribute resolution and caching guidance:
- Adopt a two-tier attribute cache: (1) hot in-memory LRU with TTL (100–500ms) at edge/serving nodes, (2) regional backing cache with stronger consistency guarantees (seconds).
- For critical attributes (billing tier, enterprise entitlements), push them as claims into short-lived JWTs during token issuance to avoid on-path lookups.
- Provide a streaming policy-delta feed (ordered, versioned) so regionals can apply revisions and maintain a policy-version watermark.

Observability and test harness requirements:
- Decision traces: every enforcement point should emit a compact decision trace (decision-id, policy-version, matched-rules, attribute-refs). Traces should be joinable with request traces.
- Sampling and full-log modes: default sampling at 0.5% for production, rampable to 100% during rollouts and incident triage.
- Regression detection: define canary prompt sets / policy predicates that exercise both allow and deny paths; attach automated quality checks to policy rollouts.
- Synthetic traffic: run region-local test clients that exercise negative cases (should be denied) and verify both enforcement and audit logs.

Failure and rollback playbook (summary):
1) If policy-induced latency exceeds SLOs on ingress or serving, automatically flip to pre-approved fallback policy bundle (pre-compiled, minimal ruleset) and notify SRE + policy owners.
2) If denial rates spike for a given tenant: tag the tenant for immediate policy review, run targeted replay on a staging PDP with captured attributes, and if necessary revert to prior policy-version.
3) For control-plane outage: allow local caches to continue honoring last-known-good policy with TTL; stream telemetry indicating operating-on-stale-policy.

Experiment matrix (priority):
- A/B compare edge-RBAC-only vs edge-RBAC+cached-ABAC for latency and false-deny rates on a subset of customers.
- Canary the policy-delta feed to a single region and measure policy convergence time and decision-consistency across regions.
- Simulate PDP throttling and measure serving node behavior when attribute lookups fail.

Open questions / TODOs:
- What is the acceptable staleness window for sensitive entitlements? (1s, 5s, 30s?)
- How do we index policy logs to make post-hoc audits cost-effective at scale?
- Should we support policy-level SLIs (e.g., decision-staleness, average-decision-latency) surfaced in the Console?
- Derive a long-term plan to unify policy authoring between Hosted and Private planes while preserving customer-managed secrets for private deployments.

Actionable next steps:
- Pair with identity team to enumerate attributes that can be pushed as JWT claims — ticket: INFRA-1123.
- Implement a minimal decision-id header and sampling pipeline for ingress; target spike test by end of Q1.
- Prototype pre-compiled tiny-DAG execution in a serving worker (spike: resource impact measurement).

Notes / context snippets from earlier discussions:
- "Prefer to keep the hot-path checks tiny; we've measured 2ms of extra latency kills small-llm use-cases." — SRE sync 2025-10-21.
- "Enterprise customers want an auditable deny trail more than low microsecond latencies for admin APIs." — Solutions eng, 2025-09.

Appendix (short):
- Decision-id header format suggestion: Redwood-DecId=v1:<region>:<policyVersion>:<randomSuffix>
- Policy-versioning scheme: semantic with build hash + monotonic publish sequence (e.g., 2026.02.1-345ab).

End of draft.
